title: Causes of WWI
group: HIST-TOPIC — Overview Anchors (each links to deeper subdomains)
examples: What was the role of the assassination in starting the war?
Can you explain how the alliance system made the war bigger?
How did the competition for colonies cause tension?

explain.say: Today we learn about the causes of the First World War.

items: Militarism: building up armies and weapons

explain.say: Militarism meant countries built huge armies and navies.
Alliances were treaties promising military support to friends.
Imperialism was the fight for colonies and resources overseas.
Nationalism was intense pride in one's own nation's culture.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparked the crisis.

faq.q: What was the main cause of the war?
faq.a: Most historians point to the combination of MAIN factors. These long-term tensions made war very likely.

faq.q: How did the alliance system work?
faq.a: It meant that if one country fought another, its allies were obligated to join the fight too.
asks: Did alliances force countries to fight?
What was the chain reaction effect?

faq.a: Nations needed raw materials and markets to fuel their growing industries, leading to conflict.
asks: Did Britain and Germany fight over land?
What did they want from colonies?

faq.q: What is the difference between nationalism and patriotism?
faq.a: Patriotism is loving your home country; nationalism can be an aggressive belief in your nation's superiority.
asks: How is it different from love of country?

faq.q: Was the assassination the real cause?
faq.a: No, the assassination was the spark. The underlying tensions from MAIN were already building up the powder keg.

facts: Militarism involved building up large standing armies and navies.
The alliance system created a chain reaction effect when war started.
Imperialism was the competition for resources and markets globally.
Nationalism fueled desires for self-rule in many groups.

quiz.say: The desire for a nation to govern itself is best described as:
quiz.why: Nationalism is the belief that a group should have its own independent state.

wrong.0: This refers to building up armies, not political belief.
wrong.1: This is about controlling foreign lands, not internal identity.
wrong.2: These are agreements between states, not an internal feeling.

quiz.say: The intense buildup of weapons and armies is called:
quiz.why: Militarism is the policy of building up military power.

wrong.1: Imperialism focuses on economic control of territories.
wrong.2: This is a political or cultural feeling, not a military policy.
wrong.3: Alliances are agreements, not the act of building weapons.

quiz.say: The competition between major powers for colonies was a key factor known as:
quiz.why: Imperialism describes the drive to acquire colonies for resources and power.

wrong.0: While militarism was present, imperialism describes the goal of the competition.
wrong.1: Alliances were the result of the competition, not the competition itself.
wrong.3: This was just the immediate trigger, not the main underlying cause.
